records.note: 'Short-duration psychedelics ... will be especially important in driving access and scale': no metric, series, threshold, regulator, product or date. 'We hopefully have both MDMA and psilocybin approved' over the next 12 months states a hope, not an expectation: 'hopefully' is not a lexicon phrase, so no bin can be set from the words (same treatment as angermayer-0002, 'R-ketamine hopefully on the market'). Both events would be writable (E-0001, FDA approval of midomafetamine for PTSD; E-0003, FDA approval of a psilocybin drug product, as an 'A and B' split) with deadline 2025-04-15 ('over the next 12 months', statement date plus 12 months), and the second would be affiliated (Compass Pathways investor); that alternative is logged. Auto-caption errors ('soloc cybin', 'game Cher') are transcription, not the forecaster's words. 'Game changer' is a slogan and is not read.

Two claims, both rejected, so one record. (a) 'All the other psychedelics which atai is doing will come to Market' two to four years after MDMA and psilocybin: 'all' is a quantifier over a set the words do not define, 'come to market' names no deciding body (a regulator's approval or atai's own launch), and the horizon is relative to an undated event (the MDMA and psilocybin approvals hoped for in angermayer-0073), so no deadline can be anchored. A coder who reads the clause as 'at least one atai psychedelic is approved' would map it to E-0029 (affiliated, undated); that reading is logged but changes 'all' to 'any'. (b) 'The landscape for mental health treatments will be really radically different' five years from now is a slogan with no observable event; 'let's say 5 years from now' (2029-04-15) could anchor a deadline, but no event can be written for it. Auto-caption 'Mia Tha' = atai is transcription.

records.note: Split of a compound claim: this record is the approval half ('portfolio of medications ... be approved over the next three to four years'); the valuation half is angermayer-0075-b. A regulator, not atai, decides approval, so the item is admitted and mapped to E-0029 (a major regulator approves an atai psychedelic therapeutic), with the reading that 'a portfolio ... be approved' is satisfied at minimum by the approval of one atai psychedelic therapeutic (the weakest reading the words support; a reading that requires every program's approval would need a set the words do not define). Affiliated: atai Life Sciences, where the forecaster is co-founder and chairman. Deadline: 'over the next ... three to four years' is read through the 'within N years' anchor at the outer bound of the range, statement date plus 4 years = 2028-04-15; a coder who takes the lower bound would set 2027-04-15, and that alternative is logged. Bin: the claim sentence contains 'going to be ... approved' (bin A) and 'very likely I believe it as well' (bin B); the strongest phrase in the sentence decides, so bin A, asserts true. The auto-caption is garbled ('a Tai', 'according to society'); the reading of 'very likely' as an attributed consensus view that the forecaster endorses is logged, and a coder who treats 'very likely' as a self-correction of 'going to be' would code B. Not KNOWN: no atai approval existed.

Valuation half of the split claim (approval half at angermayer-0075-a): 'atai should be a multi-billion company even in current markets today and not a 400 million company'. 'Multi-billion' gives no usable threshold ('multi' is a quantifier without a number, as with 'several billion' in angermayer-0019), and 'should be ... today' is a present-tense valuation opinion (undervalued now) rather than a forecast of a future price, so it also fails the expectation test. The registry's E-0028 (market capitalization at or above USD 10 billion) is not reached by these words. A share price is set by the market, so the failure is vagueness, not CONTROL.

Same statement in the same post as angermayer-0076: 'new trials can overcome the shortcomings of this package and potentially result in ultimate approval' restates, in the following paragraph, the claim that MDMA gets approved after a new Phase 3 trial program (E-0001 conditional on E-0022). The first row (angermayer-0076) stands. If it were coded separately, 'can ... potentially' would set bin C, and two items from one post on the same conditional event with different bins would double-count the post; that is why the second capture is treated as a duplicate.

Comparative without a benchmark: 'those who believe psychedelics will have a slow roll out will be very positively surprised' names no product, metric, series, threshold or date; 'roll out' is not defined. Same test as angermayer-0009, which it restates in a new source.

'$atai ... maintains high conviction in the ongoing COMP005 and COMP006 Phase 3 studies' names no outcome: the sentence does not say the trials will meet their primary endpoints, read out by a date, or support approval, so a trial_result event would be written from an implication, not the words.
